The Solo Developer Making Seven Figures From Free Browser Games
Skip to content
NAAVIK GAMING PODCAST
The Solo Developer Making Seven Figures From Free Browser Games
By Kalie Moore   •   October 13, 2026
Most studios have teams, funding, and a publisher behind them.
Abe Train
has a laptop and a handful of contractors. In this episode,
Kalie Moore
sits down with Abe, founder of Trainwreck Labs, to unpack how a former head of business intelligence at HelloFresh became one of the most successful independent developers in daily browser games. Abe quit his job on the last day of 2021 with about six months of runway, and a month later Wordle took over the internet. He built Globle, a daily geography guessing game, posted it to one Reddit community, and watched it climb to over a million players a day at its peak. They get into why that post worked when the identical one in a bigger subreddit got zero traction, why most Wordle clones vanished while Globle stuck, and why the best creator marketing he’s ever had came from people he never spoke to, including a Thai TikToker playing an English word game and a biology teacher who plays Metazooa on camera every day.
The conversation also covers how Abe has built a catalog of daily educational games as the only full-time employee. He explains why a small, obsessive audience is more valuable than a big casual one, why players always ask for games to get easier but never harder, and what he learned moderating taxonomy debates in his Discord. On monetization, he shares why he almost refused to run ads, why players barely noticed when he did, and the rule he brought from HelloFresh about the complaints you never hear. He also walks through how he barely writes code anymore, why there’s no AI-generated art in any of his games, what he learned shutting down his newsletter, and his plans for native apps, real-world events, and the Trainwreck Club subscription he gives to teachers for free.

Welcome to the Naavik Gaming Podcast. I'm your host, Kalie Moore. Most of the studios we talk about on this show have teams, funding, a publisher or platform behind them. Today's guest has none of that. He has a laptop, a handful of contractors, and has created 17 browser-based games that millions of people play without downloading a single thing.
Abe Train has spent his early career at HelloFresh, where he started as a meat buyer and worked his way up to head of business intelligence. In December of 2021, he left to build something a little bit more technical. A month later, Wordle took over the internet. He built Globle, a daily geography guessing game, posted it to Reddit, and watched it take off.
Since then, he's built over a dozen games under TrainWreck Labs, including MetaZoa, a daily biology game where players climb the tree of life. He is the only full-time employee, and over the past three years, his total revenue has passed seven figures. What makes this story especially timely is how Abe builds now.
He barely writes code himself anymore, and every jump in AI capability feels like hiring a new employee. He's also planning native apps, running real-world events based on his games, and building a subscription business on top of free games. Today, we're gonna talk about what it takes to build independent games after a viral hit, how to market and monetize browser-based games, and how close we really are to that $1 billion gaming company led by one person. Abe, welcome to the podcast.
Abe:
Hi, Kalie. Thank you so much for having me, and thank you for the lovely intro.

I want to hear about that moment of how long you thought about leaving, like, when you really made the decision, and kind of what your goals were when you left.

Yeah, absolutely. HelloFresh was an incredible experience and opportunity, and I'm really grateful for it.
